title: Existence of an integral basis for a finite extension of local coefficient fields
statement: Let $\ell$ be a prime and let $E\subseteq F$ be finite extensions of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], with the compatible absolute values extending the $\ell$-adic absolute value. Put $\mathcal O_E=\{x\in E:|x|\leq1\}$ and $\mathcal O_F=\{x\in F:|x|\leq1\}$, the rings of integers, with the inclusion induced by $E\subseteq F$. Let $d=[F:E]=\dim_E F$. There exist elements $b_1,\ldots,b_d\in\mathcal O_F$ such that every $x\in\mathcal O_F$ has a unique expression $x=\sum_{i=1}^d a_i b_i$ with $a_i\in\mathcal O_E$.

mathlib_candidate.how: Lines 175, 183, 192 give generic finite/free/rank results for integral closures. Applying them requires a theorem identifying the absolute-value ring of integers O_F with the integral closure of O_E in F, and the DVR/fraction-field/separability hypotheses. This bridge is not a one-line specialization, so this is not a Mathlib leaf.

proof.text: Write $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $B=\mathcal O_F$. Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] separately to $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$: $A$ and $B$ are subrings of their fields and $A$ is a DVR. In particular $A$ is a principal ideal domain by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and [lem-weil-pbc-pid-noetherian-normal] makes $A$ Noetherian. Compatibility gives $|a|_F=|a|_E\leq1$ for $a\in A$, so $A\subseteq B$ and multiplication makes $B$ an $A$-module. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete], $E$ is complete. By [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] and compatibility, $0<|\ell|_E=|\ell|_F=\ell^{-1}<1$; hence the norm on $E$ is nontrivial.

source.place: Opening sentence: DVR and Noetherian base ring; hypotheses for the coordinate argument

proof.text: Choose an $E$-vector-space basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $F$, and write $c_i(x)\in E$ for its coordinates. The field topologies are Hausdorff. Addition and the action $E\times F\to F$ are continuous: the latter is multiplication in $F$ composed with the inclusion of $E$, which is isometric by compatibility. Finite products give the same properties for $E^d$. Step 1 verifies that the scalar field $E$ is complete and nontrivially normed. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-linear-homeomorphism] with scalar field $E$, $V=F$, $W=E^d$, and the coordinate $E$-linear equivalence $F\xrightarrow{\sim}E^d$; it makes that equivalence continuous. The inverse image of the open set $\{(a_i):|a_i|_E<1\text{ for all }i\}$ is therefore a neighborhood of zero, so there is $\varepsilon>0$ such that $|y|_F<\varepsilon$ implies $|c_i(y)|_E<1$ for every $i$.

source.place: Opening sentence: finite-dimensional coordinate topology used to prove module finiteness

proof.text:
Choose $N\geq0$ with $\ell^{-N}<\varepsilon$, possible because $\ell>1$ and $\ell^{-N}\to0$. For every $x\in B$, $|\ell^N x|_F=\ell^{-N}|x|_F\leq\ell^{-N}<\varepsilon$, whence $\ell^N c_i(x)=c_i(\ell^Nx)\in A$. Consequently
$$x=\sum_{i=1}^d (\ell^Nc_i(x))(\ell^{-N}v_i)\in L:=\sum_{i=1}^d A(\ell^{-N}v_i).$$
This proves $B\subseteq L$ for one fixed finitely generated $A$-module $L\subseteq F$, uniformly for all $x\in B$. Because $B$ is already an $A$-submodule of $F$, it is an $A$-submodule of $L$.

source.place: Opening sentence: explicit uniform lattice bound proving finiteness; elementary consequence of step 2

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite] to the Noetherian ring $A$, the finitely generated module $L$, and its submodule $B$. This proves that $B$ is finitely generated over $A$. It is torsion-free: if $0\neq a\in A$ and $ax=0$ for $x\in B$, this equality in the field $F$ gives $x=0$. The DVR property from step 1 and [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] now show that $B$ is finite free over $A$. Choose a finite $A$-basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$; this already gives existence and uniqueness of $A$-coordinates on $B$, with $r$ still to be identified.

source.place: Tag 0AUW (lemma-dedekind-torsion-free-flat), part (3); submodule finiteness is Algebra Tag 00IK (lemma-Noetherian-basic)

proof.text: The same $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ span $F$ over $E$. Indeed, for any $y\in F$, choose $M\geq0$ with $\ell^{-M}|y|_F\leq1$. Then $\ell^My\in B$ has an expression $\sum_j a_jb_j$ with $a_j\in A$, and division by $\ell^M$ gives $y=\sum_j(\ell^{-M}a_j)b_j$ with coefficients in $E$. They are also $E$-linearly independent. Given $\sum_j u_jb_j=0$ with $u_j\in E$, choose $M\geq0$ large enough that $\ell^{-M}|u_j|_E\leq1$ simultaneously for the finitely many $j$. Then $\ell^Mu_j\in A$, so the $A$-linear independence gives $\ell^Mu_j=0$ for every $j$ and therefore $u_j=0$. These choices use the same geometric-sequence limit as step 3 and $|\ell|=\ell^{-1}$ from step 1. Thus the $b_j$ form an $E$-basis of $F$.

source.place: Opening sentence: explicit full-rank check after freeness; no localization comparison is assumed

proof.text: By [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], the cardinality $r$ of the $E$-basis in step 5 is $\dim_E F=d$. Reindex the finite $A$-basis from step 4 by $1,\ldots,d$. Its elements lie in $B=\mathcal O_F$ and the defining existence and uniqueness of its $A$-coordinates give exactly $x=\sum_{i=1}^d a_ib_i$ with $a_i\in\mathcal O_E$ for each $x\in\mathcal O_F$.
